LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation, part of Strand 2 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What is the importance of punctuation in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify punctuation marks in written sentences for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use punctuation marks in sentences for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of punctuation in writing for communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify punctuation marks in written sentences for information,

   Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use punctuation marks in sentences for effective communication,

   Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the role of punctuation in writing for communication.

   Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to copy sentences and underline the punctuation marks (full stops, comma and capital letters) in sentences,

2. share tasks to rewrite the punctuation marks on flash cards,

3. discuss the use of commas, full stops and capital letters in sentences,

4. write simple sentences using the punctuation marks (the comma, the full stop and capital letters) appropriately,

5. share their written sentences with peers for review,

6. work collaboratively to identify correct and incorrect use of punctuation marks in short passages,

7. create a short paragraph on weather with correct punctuation.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to copy sentences and underline the punctuation marks (full stops, comma and capital letters) in sentences,
2. share tasks to rewrite the punctuation marks on flash cards,
3. discuss the use of commas, full stops and capital letters in sentences,
4. write simple sentences using the punctuation marks (the comma, the full stop and capital letters) appropriately,
5. share their written sentences with peers for review,
6. work collaboratively to identify correct and incorrect use of punctuation marks in short passages,
7. create a short paragraph on weather with correct punctuation.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts when creating a short paragraph

with correct punctuation.

• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when identifying

correct and incorrect use of punctuation marks in a passage.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates varied ideas from peers when discussing the use of punctuation

marks in sentences.

• Love: This is enhanced as the learner shares their opinions during peer reviews to improve on each other’s work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is promoted as the learner appreciates different aspects of the weather in their day-to-day

experiences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of punctuation to their learning in Kiswahili and English.

Main points to remember:

1. identify punctuation marks in written sentences for information,
2. use punctuation marks in sentences for effective communication,
3. appreciate the role of punctuation in writing for communication.

Remember the key question: What is the importance of punctuation in writing?
